T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [YES] — AI valuation duration risk, fiscal deficit pressure, structural yield floor

**Synopsis:**
The article warns that rising 10-year Treasury yields (now at 4.79%, up 80bps since March 2026) are becoming an increasing headwind for US equities as the earnings season buffer fades. While strong corporate profit growth has cushioned stocks so far (S&P 500 +11% YTD), market participants flag the 5% yield level as a critical psychological and valuation threshold. Key drivers of the yield rise include sticky inflation, ballooning fiscal deficit, oil price spikes from US-Iran tensions, and hawkish signals from new Fed Chair Kevin Warsh. Analysts highlight elevated duration risk in AI-driven equity valuations, P/E cap risk, and tightening financial conditions as yield pressures persist.
